II- Arabica is a variety of coffee.

• **Hence Statement 1 is correct.**
 
 
 
• **Arabica, Robusta and Liberica** are three common coffee beans used globally and they vary in flavour, price, body and caffeine content.
 
 
• Hence Statement 2 is correct.
 
 
 
• **The Arabica is a variety of coffee is initially brought from Yemen.**
 
• The Geographical Indications Registry has granted the Geographical Indication (GI) tag to **Coorg Arabica Coffee(Karnataka),** Wayanad Robusta Coffee(Kerela), Chikmagalur Arabica Coffee(Karnataka), Araku Valley Arabica Coffee(Andhra Pradesh), and Bababudangiris Arabica Coffee(Karnataka)

questions.question: Which of the following states is the biggest producer of Pulses?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Madhya Pradesh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Madhya Pradesh** is the largest producer of pulses in India.
 
• The state contributes significantly to the total production of pulses in the country.
 
• The major pulses grown in Madhya Pradesh include chickpeas (gram), pigeon peas (arhar/tur), lentils, and moong beans.
 
• Madhya Pradesh has favorable climatic conditions and soil types that support the cultivation of a variety of pulses.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pulses**

 
 
• Pulses are an important group of crops that belong to the legume family.
 
• They are a rich source of protein, dietary fiber, vitamins, and minerals, making them an essential part of a balanced diet.
 
• Pulses are also known for their ability to fix nitrogen in the soil, which improves soil fertility and reduces the need for chemical fertilizers.
 
• Common types of pulses include chickpeas, lentils, beans, peas, and pigeon peas.
 
 
 
• **Agriculture in Madhya Pradesh**
 
 
• Madhya Pradesh is known as the "Heart of India" due to its geographical location.
 
• The state has a diverse agro-climatic condition that supports the cultivation of a wide range of crops.
 
• Apart from pulses, Madhya Pradesh is also a leading producer of wheat, soybean, and oilseeds in India.
 
• The state government has implemented various agricultural schemes and policies to support farmers and enhance agricultural productivity.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Pulses in India**
 
 
• India is the largest producer and consumer of pulses in the world.
 
• Pulses play a crucial role in ensuring food security and nutrition in the country.
 
• They are a key component of the Indian diet, especially for vegetarians who rely on pulses as a primary source of protein.
 
• The cultivation of pulses also contributes to sustainable agricultural practices and environmental conservation.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a kharif crop?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Wheat**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Wheat is primarily a **rabi crop**.
 
• Rabi crops are sown in **winter** and harvested in the spring.
 
• Wheat typically requires **cooler weather** and a moderate amount of water during the growing season.
 
• Examples of other rabi crops include **barley, mustard, and peas**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kharif Crops**

 
 
• Kharif crops, also known as monsoon crops, are sown with the beginning of the first rains in July, during the southwest monsoon season.
 
• They require a lot of water and hot weather for their growth.
 
• Examples of kharif crops include **Paddy, Soyabean, Maize, Cotton, and Groundnut**.
 
• The harvesting season for kharif crops is typically from September to October.
 
 
 
• **Rabi Crops**
 
 
• Rabi crops are sown in winter from October to December.
 
• They are harvested in the spring from April to June.
 
• Rabi crops require a warm climate for germination and a cold climate for growth.
 
• Examples of rabi crops include **Wheat, Barley, Mustard, and Peas**.
 
 
 
• **Difference Between Kharif and Rabi Crops**
 
 
• The main difference lies in the timing of their sowing and harvesting seasons.
 
• Kharif crops are dependent on the arrival of the monsoon, whereas rabi crops are grown in the winter season when the monsoon has retreated.
 
• Kharif crops need a lot of water and hot weather, while rabi crops require cold weather for growth and less water.
 
 
 
• **Important Indian Cropping Seasons**
 
 
• India has two main cropping seasons - Rabi and Kharif, and a third, less significant one called Zaid.
 
• Zaid crops are grown between March and June, in the intervening period between the rabi and kharif seasons.
 
• Examples of zaid crops include **watermelon, cucumber, and fodder crops**.

questions.question: In West Bengal, how many rice crops are grown in a year?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Three**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In West Bengal, rice is a major crop and is cultivated three times a year.
 
• The three main rice crops are known as Aus, Aman, and Boro.
 
• Aus rice is sown during the pre-monsoon season (March-April) and harvested in the summer (June-July).
 
• Aman rice is sown during the monsoon season (June-July) and harvested in the winter (November-December).
 
• Boro rice is sown during the winter season (December-January) and harvested in the summer (April-May).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Aus Rice:**

 
 
• Also known as autumn rice, it is one of the early varieties of rice cultivated in the pre-monsoon period.
 
• It is typically sown in March-April and harvested by June-July.
 
• This variety of rice requires less water compared to the other two, making it suitable for areas with less rainfall.
 
 
 
• **Aman Rice:**
 
 
• Also known as winter rice, it is a monsoon-season crop.
 
• It is sown in June-July and harvested by November-December.
 
• This variety of rice depends heavily on the monsoon rains for its cultivation.
 
 
 
• **Boro Rice:**
 
 
• Also known as summer rice, it is cultivated in the winter season.
 
• It is sown in December-January and harvested by April-May.
 
• This variety requires irrigation facilities as it is grown during the dry season.

questions.question: Cotton requires ______ temperature, light rainfall or irrigation, ______ frost-free days and bright sun-shine for its growth.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**high, 210.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Cotton thrives in **high temperatures**, which promotes** optimal growth and development.**
 
• It requires l**ight rainfall **or proper irrigation to provide the necessary moisture for its growth.
 
• Cotton cultivation requires a significant number of frost-free days,** typically around 210, **to ensure the plant's survival and uninterrupted growth.
 
• **Bright sunshine** is crucial for cotton plants as they require ample sunlight for photosynthesis, which is essential for their growth and the production of cotton fibres.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kharif crops**

 
 
• Kharif Crops are** planted at the onset of the South-West monsoon,** primarily in** India, Pakistan, and Bangladesh,** during the rainy season. 
 
• The sowing of these crops takes place between the months of **June and July. **
 
• Upon reaching maturity, typically in October, these crops are **harvested in the Autumn season. **
 
• Examples of Kharif crops include **rice, cotton, corn, sugarcane, turmeric, pigeon pea, and more.**
 
 
 
• **Rabi crops**
 
 
• Rabi Crops are** cultivated during the winter season **in regions with a subtropical climate.
 
• They include important crops like **wheat, barley, oats, chickpeas, and peas.**
 
• The **Sowing of Rabi crops** takes place between **October and December**.
 
• These crops** require cooler temperatures and lesser rainfall** compared to Kharif crops.
 
• Rabi crops play a crucial role in ensuring food security and contribute significantly to the agricultural economy.
 
 
 
• **Zaid crops**
 
 
• Zaid Crops are **grown during the summer season** in regions with a **tropical climate**.
 
• These crops are typically** cultivated between the months of March and June.**
 
• Zaid crops are known for their **quick growth and shorter duration** compared to Kharif and Rabi crops.
 
• Examples of Zaid crops include **cucumber, watermelon, bitter gourd, and cowpea.**
 
• These crops are often irrigated using modern techniques and are harvested before the onset of the monsoon season.

questions.question: Which state of India is given the popular name of 'India's bread-basket'?
questions.solution:

• **Punjab**__ and Haryana region are considered the breadbaskets of India.
 
• It is called India's bread-basket because in the 1.5 percent of India's land area Punjab produces 20% of India's wheat.
